question_patterns_used.name: Definition
question_patterns_used.lesson_response: Places each exact controlled definition in a separately anchored block, then distinguishes the comparison each definition makes.

question_patterns_used.name: Comparison
question_patterns_used.lesson_response: Uses grouped readings, a known true value and instrument capability to separate precision, accuracy and resolution.

question_patterns_used.name: Measurement selection
question_patterns_used.lesson_response: Uses a new wire-diameter scenario to choose resolution appropriate to an intended change, without copying a paper question.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped part directly asks what accuracy means.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: State accuracy using closeness to a true value.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Identify true value as the comparison point, not agreement among repeats.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Calling repeated close readings accurate without a true-value comparison.
lesson_sections_informed: Accuracy means closeness to the true value

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped wire-diameter part asks students to distinguish precision and accuracy in a practical context.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Separate repeatability, instrument reading detail and closeness to a true diameter.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Compare readings with each other for precision and a measured value with the true diameter for accuracy.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Treating a small scale division as proof that the measurement is accurate.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped part explicitly asks for the difference between accuracy and precision.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Give both criteria without swapping range and true value.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Assign range to precision and true value to accuracy.
lesson_sections_informed: Three questions to ask about a measurement

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped part links a precision definition to micrometer-versus-metre-rule selection.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Explain why a finer smallest division supports a more suitable measurement.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Match the size of the required detail to instrument resolution.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Assuming a more finely divided instrument automatically removes every error.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped part gives repeated values with a stated true value and asks for precise-but-not-accurate reasoning.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Use both small spread and a large true-value discrepancy in one explanation.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: First judge range, then compare representative result with the true value.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Treating a small range as evidence of accuracy.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped part isolates the meaning of low precision.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Explain wide spread rather than merely name the term.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Identify disagreement among repeated class results.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Describing low precision as a shared offset from the true value.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped part selects an instrument for a stated length measurement.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Choose apparatus compatible with the demanded measurement detail.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Compare expected detail with the instrument's reading capability.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Selecting a coarse scale because it can cover the length range.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped part asks what precise means when the set is not accurate.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: State small range or close grouping independently of accuracy.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Restrict the answer to agreement among readings.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Adding closeness to the true value to a precision-only answer.

definitions_considered.exact_text: the degree of agreement among repeated measurements, indicated by their spread or range
the closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity
the smallest change in a quantity that a measuring instrument can distinguish, usually set by its smallest scale division
